bug: Checkpoint load/save decisions consulted the overridable public closed getter instead of private terminal state. A false shadow allowed load publication after closure and digest work after closure; true or throwing shadows could reject live operations or throw instead of returning a typed failure.

before.observations: Four scenarios were tested against false, true and throwing own-property status getters: live empty load, live save, closed save, and closure during load digest. All twelve failed behavior or no-public-read assertions.

fix: Use private terminal state at empty-load publication, verified-load publication and save admission.
Preserve the existing connection failure code at those sites and the outcome semantics of writes already dispatched.

verification.typecheck: passed (runtime, unit tests and browser tests)

scenarios: Closure during real Web Crypto digest returns a connection failure despite a false public status getter; a subsequent save does no additional digest work and neither operation invokes the getter.
Closing a store releases loads queued behind blocked database deletion.
An explicit checkpoint survives real page reload with Undo/Redo.
A full session backup restores typed values and the redo frontier through Rust.

limits: This is lifecycle robustness for integrations, not isolation from arbitrary same-origin code.
Closing a store still cannot cancel native digest or already-dispatched IndexedDB work. Load publication waits for digest settlement, then rejects a closed owner.
No durable format, Rust implementation, package version or release budget changed.
The separate WebKit numeric fault remains unresolved; native instrumentation stayed paused.
No full release qualification, commit, push or publication is claimed.
